Across five studies tracking content through AI transmission chains, three steady patterns emerge. The work asks how relay transforms content, not merely whether it degrades it.

First, convergence pulls texts toward a shared default of moderate confidence, muted affect and analytical structure. Second, selective survival keeps narrative anchors while stripping evidence texture, hedges, quotes and attributions. Third, competitive filtering lets strong arguments survive while weaker yet valid views vanish. Human readers rated relayed content as more credible and polished, yet showed worse factual recall, weaker balance perception and dulled emotional resonance.
arxiv-2602-18274:
Viktoriia Makovska and four co-authors teach data design as group work, not a solo technical task. Their 2026 paper notes that entity-relationship diagrams shape how data systems picture people, work, and groups, yet classes usually teach the skill as pure technique. Research on joint design shows that bringing varied voices into the work brings out hidden knowledge and challenges quiet assumptions.

The team introduces GARLIC, a workshop format that adapts the earlier ONION joint-design frame into role-play, joint building, guided critique, and repeated revision. GARLIC builds both design skill and a critical eye for the social and ethical stakes of how data pictures people. It lowers the entry barrier to joint design work and gives students hands-on practice in shared, inclusive design.
arxiv-2602-18774:
Test coverage for code usually means covering every edge of a control-flow graph, but real test plans also impose rules about order, such as flows that must or must not happen. Jakub Ruszil, with three co-authors, studies in 2026 how five such constraint types change whether an edge-covering test set exists and how hard it is to find.

Positive constraints demand at least one path with one vertex before another, negative constraints forbid any such path. Once, max-once, and always constraints tighten how often or how universally that order appears. Positive constraints stay decidable in polynomial time, while the other four are NP-complete, even on acyclic graphs, by reductions from variants of SAT. A fixed-parameter algorithm for negative constraints offers a practical foothold despite that hardness.
arxiv-2602-18874:
Generating a new Chinese character in a target font style from only a few examples is a hard disentangling problem. Jie Li, with three co-authors, presents SLD-Font in 2026. It is a structure-level disentangled diffusion model for few-shot Chinese font generation.

Content and style enter through two separate channels. SimSun-style images serve as content templates, joined to noisy latent features. Style features from a CLIP model enter through cross-attention. A background noise removal module cleans complex stroke regions in pixel space. Only style-related modules are fine-tuned, which adapts the model to new styles without overfitting to reference content. New Grey and OCR metrics judge content quality. Tests show higher style fidelity with comparable content accuracy.
arxiv-2602-18974:
Stellarator coils are expensive, and their distance from the plasma surface drives cost, size, and engineering difficulty. John Kappel, with three co-authors, asks in 2026 whether a simple magnetic quantity predicts coil complexity for filamentary coils. The smallest magnetic gradient scale length on the last closed flux surface has already proved a good proxy for minimum coil-surface distance in current-potential optimisations.

The authors test whether the same holds for filament coils, and whether the scale length works as an optimisation objective. Analyses of single-stage-optimised equilibria, quasihelically symmetric optimisations with coil continuation and alpha-particle tracing, and finite-beta equilibria with random boundaries all point the same way. The scale length correlates with minimum coil-surface and coil-coil distances when sufficient coil length is allowed. Optimising it can even improve confinement with coils present, up to a point, though trade-offs with confinement proxies remain.
arxiv-2602-19374:
Jacek Jendrej and Tony Salvi study the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a gauge-invariant polynomial nonlinearity. For small, localized starting data with finite energy and low regularity, they prove solutions exist globally, with the profile staying compact. In plain terms, small waves neither blow up nor spread their core structure away over time.

The paper also derives the long-term expansion of such solutions to any order, accounting for long-range effects from the cubic part. This is a careful account of adjusted scattering, describing how solutions resemble free waves only after a correction. The analysis rests on the space-time resonance method, a tool for tracking interacting waves.
arxiv-2602-19874:
Recognizing social behaviour in animals from video has advanced, but accurate three-dimensional pose and shape have lagged, above all for non-human primates. A 2026 arXiv paper by Lucas Martini and four co-authors introduces BigMaQ, a large data set of interacting rhesus macaques with detailed three-dimensional pose descriptions.

The set holds over seven hundred scenes, built by fitting a high-quality macaque template mesh onto single monkeys as textured avatars. That yields pose descriptions more accurate than prior surface-based tracking for animals. A derived benchmark, BigMaQ500, ties surface-based pose vectors to individual frames for action recognition. Pairing standard image and video features with the new pose descriptors lifts recognition scores substantially. The data set is the first to weave dynamic pose-shape information into animal action recognition at this scale.
arxiv-2602-19974:
Image generators can produce beautiful pictures that still get spatial relationships wrong, with objects in impossible arrangements. A 2026 arXiv paper by Tianyu Wang and five co-authors proposes RL-RIG, a reinforcement learning framework that reasons about space through reflection.

The architecture follows a generate-reflect-edit loop with four parts: a diffuser, a checker, an actor, and an inverse diffuser, designed to spark chain-of-thought reasoning in image generation. A reflection-based training method teaches the actor to write edit prompts and the editor to improve quality under a given prompt. Evaluation prioritizes spatial accuracy, using scene-graph overlap and a vision-language model as judge on a scene-graph data set. Results beat leading open-source models by a clear margin on controllable, precise spatial reasoning.
arxiv-2602-20174:
Integer and fractional quantum Hall effects are usually treated separately. Donut-shaped sigma models of magneto-transport unify them on their own through modular symmetry. A 2026 arXiv paper by C. A. Lütken, working alone, analyzes those models through mirror symmetry, a quantum match.

Mirror symmetry maps the models to workable mirror models, also elliptic. Shape-based safety there comes from winding numbers of a more familiar kind. Phase diagrams and scaling features are compared with three decades of lab and computed data. Scaling flows drawn from quantum Hall experiments match modular forecasts well, including the spots of many quantum critical points. One standout model, perhaps the simplest and most natural, yields a spread exponent matching the computed value closely.
arxiv-2602-20374:
J. Qiu and thirteen co-authors report the first observations of gas-phase carbon dioxide absorption toward the Galactic Center with the James Webb Space Telescope. Carbon dioxide is stable and abundant, yet hard to detect without observable pure rotational transitions. Carbon dioxide sits as ice in dense clouds, appearing less often as a gas, mostly around protostars and protoplanetary systems.

Absorption appears toward two infrared-bright Galactic Center regions, with gas temperatures between twenty and fifty kelvin and zero radial velocity. Acetylene and hydrogen cyanide absorption appear alongside, with carbon dioxide ice absorption at an ice-to-gas ratio of ninety. The absorbing gas likely lies in the foreground, in one or more clumpy clouds between Earth and the center. Point-like carbon dioxide emission near a Galactic Center star, coincident with a known X-ray source, may mark a symbiotic binary.
arxiv-2602-20574:
Self-distillation assumes some trusted check on answers, yet many settings offer no ground truth labels, rewards, or outside graders. Alex Stein and two co-authors study document-grounded question answering with asymmetric context, where one model acts as both tutor and student. The tutor sees a source document during training, while the student must answer from the question alone at test time. Their method, GATES, derives supervision from tutor consensus instead of assuming tutor correctness.

The method samples many document-grounded reasoning traces and uses agreement to gate learning, then distills full tutor reasoning paths, not just final answers. That dense signal greatly lifts transfer to the document-free student. Held-out in-domain accuracy under asymmetric testing rises from forty-six percent to sixty-two percent. Average majority-vote accuracy on public document-free math benchmarks rises from about twenty percent to about thirty-five percent.
arxiv-2602-20674:
Measurement-based quantum networks rely on multipartite pre-shared entanglement to satisfy requests, yet classic designs tune resources for single tasks. Jakob Kaltoft Søndergaard and two co-authors note that many tasks may arrive at once and compete for the same links. They introduce compatibility as a design metric for whether concurrent tasks can share the same stock. They define a worst-case notion where nodes cannot coordinate after task arrival.

The paper illustrates why tasks may prove incompatible, then extends the fit to stochastic arrivals and to extra links on demand. Lack of fit, they show, differs with the set of concurrent tasks. Fit should therefore guide stock design, deciding which task pairs the network supports with pre-shared links and which need execution-time coordination. Simulations show worst-case fit gains of forty to fifty-five percent in supported tasks over the single-task baseline.
arxiv-2602-20974:
Engineering design juggles cheap, rough simulations against costly, accurate ones. Ahmed Mohamed Eisa Nasr, Ali Elham, and Haris Moazam Sheikh blend the two in this 2026 arXiv paper using MAST, a multi-fidelity surrogate model based on spatial trust-weighting. The method merges corrected low-fidelity observations with high-fidelity predictions, trusting the latter near observed samples and the former elsewhere.

Explicit discrepancy modeling plus distance-based weighting yields a single heteroscedastic Gaussian process with closed-form variance propagation. Across synthetic benchmarks, MAST beats current state-of-the-art methods and stays robust as budgets and fidelity gaps vary, conditions where rivals degrade or wobble. Readers get a spatially adaptive surrogate recipe for sparse, budget-limited settings.
arxiv-2602-21274:
Extracting a commodity optimally is harder when selling itself depresses the price. Johanna Garzon, Jhonatan Mora Rodriguez, and Harold Moreno-Franco study that problem in this 2026 arXiv paper. The agent's spot-market actions exert an additive proportional negative impact on price, while the untouched price follows a drifted Brownian motion with jumps.

The agent's aim is an extraction strategy maximizing expected net profits under those dynamics. Readers get a model where market impact and jump risk shape extraction timing together, rather than treating price as exogenous. The paper serves resource economics and stochastic control alike, with a problem that is simple to state and rich in trade-offs.
arxiv-2602-21574:
Na Li and one co-author propose and analyze a linear, unconditionally energy-stable SAV finite element method for the Cahn-Hilliard equation. That equation models phase separation with significant physical relevance and rich mathematical structure. The scheme builds on the Scalar Auxiliary Variable approach.

Convergence analysis of the fully discrete scheme under suitable regularity assumptions confirms optimal-order convergence in both time and space. The result covers the phase variable, chemical potential, and auxiliary variable in the H1 norm. The scheme is also proven unconditionally energy stable. A numerical example demonstrates the method's effectiveness and confirms the theoretical convergence rates.
arxiv-2602-21774:
L. Yildiz and two co-authors develop a dark-sector selective trace-coupled extension of gravity. Its matter-curvature coupling depends only on the trace of the dark-matter energy-momentum tensor from a canonical dark-matter field. The construction specifies the trace sector, removes the matter-Lagrangian ambiguity of f(R,T)-type models, and keeps visible matter minimally coupled. The team derives the field equations, the dark-sector exchange structure, and the scalar-perturbation system in gauge-ready form.

In the sub-horizon regime, effective modified-gravity functions govern structure growth and light deflection, and the model yields correlated, scale- and time-dependent departures from General Relativity in growth and lensing observables. A multi-probe framework built on redshift-space distortions, weak lensing, and CMB lensing targets degeneracy breaking beyond background-expansion tests. It lays action- and perturbation-level foundations for linear-regime constraints in this setting.
arxiv-2602-21874:
Dimitrios Apostolakis and four co-authors present an augmented reality interface for disaster response, built around the user. It uses 3D Gaussian Splatting to show rich scene reconstructions. At the same time, it keeps users aware of their surroundings. It also keeps mental load low. Control is light in weight. It pairs World-in-Miniature navigation with semantic Points of Interest. Those points can be filtered as needed. A design that streams updates backs the whole interface as scene models change.

Feedback from a first trial says the design is easy to use. It also supports real-time teamwork. Testers praised the controls and Points of Interest for fast choices in context. A fuller user-centred test found strong ease of use and high approval rates.
arxiv-2602-21974:
Many science and engineering problems boil down to huge equations whose unknowns are multi-way arrays called tensors. Martina Iannacito and two co-authors offer two new descent methods for solving such equations when the core operator is symmetric and positive definite. Their methods extend a recent subspace conjugate gradient approach and store tensors in the compact Tucker form, which keeps memory use down.

To speed the work further, the authors mix exact and rough arithmetic in smaller steps and add preconditioners that help the methods settle faster. They test the ideas on three-dimensional physics problems with separable coefficients and compare against a leading rival method. The new methods hold their own, giving practitioners a lighter way to solve large tensor equations.
arxiv-2602-22074:
Gravitational-wave searches usually assume detector noise follows a bell-shaped Gaussian curve, but real data carry outliers and overlapping signals that break that assumption. Argyro Sasli and six co-authors extend a robust statistical framework based on heavy-tailed likelihoods, adapting the hyperbolic likelihood method to the full frequency domain. The goal is to stay strong on clean data while holding up when noise turns messy.

Two case studies test the idea: a simulated massive black hole merger for the future LISA observatory, where the method matches the standard Whittle likelihood. A second case uses a real stellar-mass merger from ground detectors with non-Gaussian noise. In the messier real case the robust framework shows its value, handling outliers and overlaps that Gaussian methods mishandle. Analysts gain a safer default for real gravitational-wave data.
arxiv-2602-23474:
Jonathan I. Katz and one co-author propose that many transient X-ray sources are eccentric binaries in which a star transfers mass to a compact companion at periastron, the closest point of the orbit. X-rays from transferred matter evaporate material from the star, and the recoil widens the orbit and raises its eccentricity.

After each periastron passage, the system would appear as a transient X-ray source: a Galactic analogue of a tidal disruption event, but recurrent rather than catastrophic, with a gradually increasing period. The short paper thus reframes recurring X-ray outbursts as the natural outcome of mass transfer in highly eccentric binaries, linking orbital evolution to observed transient behavior.
arxiv-2602-23574:
Ruxiao Duan and one co-author present evidential neural radiance fields for doubt-aware 3D scene building. Neural radiance fields achieve strong scores in scene rebuilds and novel view making, yet lack of doubt scores limits their use in safety-key settings.

Current doubt-score methods for radiance fields fail to capture aleatoric and epistemic doubt apart. Among methods that score one or the other, many harm drawing quality or incur large compute cost to obtain doubt scores. The new chance-based method fits smoothly with radiance field drawing, giving direct scores of both doubt types from a single forward pass. Tests against multiple doubt-score methods on three standard benchmarks show state-of-the-art scene rebuild truth and doubt-score quality.
arxiv-2602-23874:
Alejandro Guerra-Manzanares and Jialin Huang benchmark how well intrusion detection features transfer across network domains for IoT botnet detection. The 2026 paper tests three widely used flow feature sets across four datasets covering varied IoT and industrial IoT conditions, with several classifiers and feature-importance analysis.

Models trained in one domain degrade sharply in another, showing how sensitive such detectors are to shifts in traffic character. Both the classifier and the feature representation strongly affect transfer, so no single choice rescues a poorly matched feature space. The authors draw practical guidelines for feature engineering under domain variability, stressing that a useful detector needs both strong in-domain accuracy and resilience to new domains. That combination is achieved through careful feature design, apt algorithm choice, and adaptive strategies. In short, a good test set in one place must still work well in a new place.
arxiv-2602-23974:
Fan Zhang and two co-authors present a pessimistic auxiliary policy for offline reinforcement learning, where agents learn only from pre-collected data. The 2026 paper notes that offline learning inevitably samples actions outside the dataset, whose value estimates carry errors that compound into large overestimation.

The auxiliary policy samples reliable actions by maximizing a lower confidence bound on the action-value function. Near the learned policy it favors actions that are both high-value and low-uncertainty, steering learning away from tempting but poorly supported actions. With fewer approximation errors entering from sampled actions, error accumulation eases. Tests on offline benchmarks show that the pessimistic auxiliary strategy improves the efficacy of other offline methods when added to them, offering a general, cautious sampling fix.
arxiv-2602-24174:
Dor Tsur and two co-authors present TASC, a task-centric acceleration framework for small language models. Small models are prized for efficiency but often run in high-volume, low-latency settings where speed still matters. The 2026 paper offers two methods: one for fine-tuning and one for inference.

TASC-ft iteratively enriches the tokenizer vocabulary with frequent output n-grams, then fine-tunes the model to use the expanded vocabulary, shortening sequences for repetitive task outputs. TASC-spec is a lightweight, training-free speculative decoding method that builds an n-gram draft model from the task's output corpus. It mixes task and context n-gram information while avoiding draft-target vocabulary alignment constraints. Tests across low output-variability generation tasks show consistent inference efficiency gains while preserving task performance, making small models faster without retraining at inference time.
arxiv-2603-00274: Reed and Salinas address a puzzle from the PREX and CREX electron scattering experiments, whose neutron-skin measurements for calcium-48 and lead-208 sit uneasily with current nuclear models. They strengthen the isovector spin-orbit part of density functional theory by adding massive spin-2 mesons to the Lagrangian. These mesons contribute meaningfully and ease problems that plagued earlier attempts to boost spin-orbit effects in finite nuclei. The authors also discuss the implications for nuclear forces and future measurements such as the Mainz Radius Experiment.
arxiv-2603-00374: Nguyen and Wellman tackle game solving from fixed data alone, where only part of the game dynamics may show in the record and a claimed equilibrium cannot even be checked. They rank candidate equilibria by their chance of low regret under the available evidence, extending Policy Space Response Oracles with uncertainty measures and a regret leaning objective. A new meta strategy solver steers search for the offline case. Tests show their COffeE PSRO method finds lower regret answers than leading offline rivals and clarifies how method parts shape game fidelity.
arxiv-2603-00574: He, Guo, and Jin tackle multi modal test time adaptation, where new test data causes negative transfer in one channel and forgetting in another. Their DASP framework first diagnoses which channel is biased, finding it carries far higher redundancy across feature dimensions. Adapters then split into stable and plastic parts: the biased side updates its plastic part, while the unbiased side skips plastic updates and tunes its stable part under KL regularisation. The asymmetric design protects stability while allowing needed plasticity.
arxiv-2603-00674: Kowalczuk studies critical ideals for countable compact spaces in the Katětov order, for ideals that characterise spaces homeomorphic to ordinal powers with the order topology. For limit ordinals, she shows the conv ideals fail to serve as greatest lower bounds of their predecessors. She therefore defines conv ideals indexed by smaller ordinals, which with the first ones form intertwined decreasing hierarchies of complete ideals at two complexity levels. Several cardinal invariants of these ideals are also computed, tying the work to recent literature.
arxiv-2603-00774: Elahimanesh and five colleagues test whether chatbot architecture shapes therapeutic dialogue across three designs grounded in Self-Attachment Technique psychotherapy. A multi agent system with a stage matched finite state machine and shared long term memory faces a single agent with identical knowledge and prompts, plus an unguided model. In an eight day trial of 66 Farsi speaking participants across three chatbots, the multi agent system feels significantly more natural and human like and leads on most other ratings. Structure matters as much as prompt wording, the findings suggest.
arxiv-2603-00874: Mandap devises a test for whether crop-quality patterns differ across mapped fields when nearby plots resemble each other. Standard tests assume independence, so spatial correlation inflates false alarms; his rank-based copula method smooths with spatial weights instead. Theory shows the statistic follows a weighted chi-squared limit, and simulations with skewed spatial data hold their stated error rate where older methods turn sharply overconfident.
arxiv-2603-01374: Plank and seven colleagues present two models used in a 2025 New Zealand winter assessment programme for SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV. SARS-CoV-2 data came from the national Covid-19 surveillance system, while influenza and RSV data were limited to a sentinel hospital programme. Run weekly from May to October 2025, the models gave a quantitative picture of the current trend, growth rate estimates, and 28-day case forecasts. Results and interpretation went weekly to public health partners in a trans-Tasman programme run by ACEFA.
arxiv-2603-01674:
Boriana Chtirkova explains why near-term warming lags behind the warming a fixed climate would reach. Her 2026 analysis treats the transient response, where forcing keeps rising, against the equilibrium response for the same forcing. The gap between them is not fixed; it shifts with time and with key climate traits.

She solves a heat equation with surface feedback under forcing that rises in a straight line. At first the surface warms more slowly than its steady-state twin, then speeds up toward a parallel path. On that path, both curves rise together with a constant offset set by forcing rate and heat capacity. Reaching that path takes thousands of years, shaped in part by ocean mixing. Over the next century, the gap grows, which matters for reading near-term change.
arxiv-2603-01874:
Tailai Song, Pedro Casas, and Michela Meo catch phishing webpages with a light model that needs no outside reference lists. Their 2026 work notes that top detectors lean on cloud services and knowledge bases, which hurts scale and reproducibility. Classic deep models, meanwhile, often fail as phishing campaigns evolve.

Their system, SpecularNet, reads only a page domain name and its HTML structure. The page tree becomes a graph, and a hierarchical autoencoder passes messages level by level along it. That design captures structural habits of phishing pages while running fast on plain CPUs. Against thirteen top detectors, scores stay competitive at a tiny fraction of the compute cost. Scores on benchmarks sit just below the best reference-based rival, with per-page checks in milliseconds, and field tests catch most live phishing sites.
arxiv-2603-02574:
Rhitankar Bandyopadhyay and Diganta Mukherjee build a fairer rating system for Test cricket in this 2026 paper. The current global ranking ignores home advantage, toss effects, and scheduling gaps. Those omissions produce inconsistent team evaluations. Their framework adapts Glicko's rating model, a probabilistic system from competitive games.

Context factors enter the ratings alongside margin of victory, a marker of dominance. The enhanced model estimates expected scores more accurately on past match data. Predictive accuracy improves over the standard approach as well. Bootstrap resampling confirms the ratings stay stable under scheduling changes. Resampled schedules barely move the rankings, which supports their robustness. The authors present the system as a fairer, more consistent basis for ranking Test teams.
arxiv-2603-02874:
Georgios Pantazopoulos compares three model families at finding and reusing information inside long inputs. Transformers excel at such in-context retrieval but grow costly as inputs lengthen. State space models process inputs in linear time yet retrieve less reliably, and hybrids mix the two designs.

Two synthetic tasks test the difference: copying a short pattern that follows a query, and a two-step lookup that ends by reporting a position. Hybrids matched or beat transformers on the dense copying task and used training data more efficiently. Transformers still won the position task outright. Probing the learned signals showed state space models place nearby positions close together in their internal space, a tidy structure that explains both their strengths and their limits.
arxiv-2603-03074:
Xiaohan Peng, Wendy Mackay, and Janin Koch redesign how creative professionals steer generative AI. Design work is nonlinear and reflective, yet most AI tools force designers to type prompts or accept whole-image changes. Their 2026 workshop paper presents three systems that spread control across different moments of the process.

DesignPrompt, FusAIn, and DesignTrace let practitioners guide intent, inputs, and process itself, rather than fixing outputs afterward. The authors argue alignment is an ongoing negotiation, not a one-shot command. The AI should sometimes lead, when the designer wants inspiration, and sometimes follow, when precise craft matters. Which role fits depends on the creative stage and the designer's current need.
arxiv-2603-03474:
Shiqi Cao counts permutations that dodge two forbidden patterns at once. The patterns are partially ordered patterns, flexible templates that each stand for whole families of classical permutation patterns. Gao and Kitaev had settled many counting problems for avoiding one such pattern. Cao's 2026 paper starts the harder joint problem, for pairs drawn from the flat pattern class.

Avoiders of these pairs connect unexpectedly to the k-Fibonacci numbers, a generalization of the famous counting sequence. A bijection to certain restricted permutations then lets Cao import an established method and derive the generating function for the avoiders. For separable permutations, the paper extends single-pattern results: joint counts by six different statistics for patterns up to length five. When both patterns have length five, the generating function is rational, with a numerator of hundreds of terms.
arxiv-2603-03874:
Xueke Chen, Xinyi Zhang, and others study thermal leptogenesis in the minimal left-right symmetric model, asking whether one measured value can explain the universe's matter excess. Leptogenesis links neutrino physics to the observed baryon asymmetry, but unknown high-energy parameters usually hide the link. In this model, with general parity as the left-right symmetry, the hermitian Dirac neutrino coupling lets the right-handed mixing matrix be fixed with minimal assumptions.

The authors show that a real right-handed mixing matrix favors CP-conserving Majorana phases, leaving the Dirac CP-violating phase as the sole source of asymmetry. Exploring all four leptogenesis scenarios numerically, they find this phase alone can make the observed asymmetry with the correct sign in set parameter regions. Results depend sensitively on neutrino mass ordering and the lightest neutrino mass, making the approach testable by future measurements.
arxiv-2603-03974: Qiu-Chen Yang and Kun Yin show strong and weak convergence rates for a slow-fast system driven by multiplicative Lévy noise. Multiplicative noise complicates exponential ergodicity of the frozen process, especially gradient figures. Two routes show exponential ergodicity, coupling arguments and a spatial periodic method, with gradient bounds from heat kernel asymptotics. Under sufficient Hölder regularity of time-linked coefficients of the slow process, they obtain an optimal strong convergence rate and a weak convergence rate of order one.
arxiv-2603-04674: Fu and colleagues model coupled charm and charmonium transport in quark-gluon plasma. Open and hidden charm bits face strong forces. The framework uses T-matrix forces with Wilson-line data from lattice QCD. The same forces and spectral functions judge charm-quark spread and hidden-charm motion jointly. The hidden-charm balance limit, key for rebirth, is judged under broad spectral functions. Charm-quark spread runs via Langevin motion. The stats model balance limit returns once charm quarks settle, and early Pb-Pb uses capture central and motion trends.
arxiv-2603-04874: Jerrin Bright and team ask how much a pitcher's body alone reveals about the coming pitch, classifying eight types from single-camera 3D pose chains without ball-flight data. Their pipeline combines a diffusion-based pose model, auto event finding, checked biomechanical features, and gradient-boosted sorting using 229 kinematic features. Across 119,561 professional pitches, body kinematics alone reach 80.4% accuracy, with upper-body mechanics carrying most of the signal and wrist position the leading cue.
arxiv-2603-04974: Biao Liu and team offer VRM, Variational Reward Building, a method teaching reward models to catch authentic human preferences instead of spurious links. Standard reward models map prompt-reply pairs to scalar scores, inviting reward hacking. Human test instead weighs high-dimensional objectives by prompt context, then judges quality through low-dimensional semantic features like logical coherence. VRM models both the objective weights and the semantic features as latent variables inferred by variational inference, with theory showing a tighter carry-over error bound than older reward models.
arxiv-2603-05074: Lingyi Wang and team build a perturbative method for the mean-squared displacement of active Brownian particles with a finite moment of inertia. From the Fokker-Planck formula, they Fourier-transform spatial coordinates and use Hermite polynomials as eigenfunctions for angular speed, letting a systematic order-by-order growth. Resumming the series in Laplace space and inverting the transform gives an explicit displacement formula depending on the moment of inertia, checked against number runs.
arxiv-2603-05774: Luo and team address spread random minimax tuning with random limits. They propose a Softmax-Weighted Switching slope method. Under full joining, oracle cost reaches order epsilon to the minus fourth. Partial joining study sizes sampling noise via an edge guess. Loosening bounds guesses, they set a tighter softmax knob bound. A unified error split and sharp log promise follow. Finally, a single-loop switching device betters worst-case scores. It bypasses knob response and swings. Tests cover Neyman-Pearson, fair sorting, and teamed learning.
arxiv-2603-06074: Sajti and Deák derive a Parratt method widened to uneven systems. Neutron and X-ray bounce study looks at thin multilayer systems. Before, the Parratt method covered even systems only. Trait tables can handle uneven problems too, but they suffer number wobbles, which may arise for thick samples at grazing angle hit. The method avoids the number wobbles of the trait table method. Formulae for both bounce-back and pass-through are derived. The new approach proves stable when results from other methods are compared.
arxiv-2603-06274: Niu and his team rethink causal attention from information flow, noting that first tokens join every later token's aggregation. Past sparse methods use one top-k choice across token spots in a layer, ignoring built-up token dependence in causal designs. Their Stem module keeps first tokens for recursive dependencies, with top-k caps that shift by spot in each layer. It favors high impact tokens by rough output size through an output aware metric. Tests show Stem reaching higher accuracy with less compute and faster pre-fill.
arxiv-2603-06774: Cain studies neural representation spaces through gauge freedom. Hidden vectors are defined only up to invertible linear maps, since downstream weights can absorb the inverse map and leave the network function unchanged. In that light, cosine similarity becomes metric-dependent, shifting under coordinate changes that preserve predictions. That single view explains unstable cosine similarity, uneven embedding spaces, and the appeal of comparison methods like SVCCA and CKA. Experiments confirm that inserted invertible maps distort cosine similarity and neighbor structure while predictions stay fixed.
arxiv-2603-06874: Olson and colleagues present LieCraft, a framework and sandbox for gauging LLM deception, fixing gaps in earlier game-based tests. At its core lies a multiplayer hidden-role game where players pick an ethical side and play strategies over a long run to finish missions. Cooperators solve challenges and expose bad actors, while Defectors dodge notice while secretly sabotaging missions. Ten grounded scenarios like childcare, hospital resources, and loan lending reset the mechanics in morally weighty, high-stakes domains. Careful mechanics and rewards balance gameplay and push meaningful strategic choices.
arxiv-2603-06974: Allen presents Elenchus, a system for knowledge base building in inferentialist semantics. Knowledge work becomes explicitation, not lifting from words or text. An expert builds a two-sided stance, claims plus denials, through prover-skeptic debate with a model foe. The model raises tensions, claims of joint clash, settled by taking back, tweaks, or fights. The model serves as a fallible proof oracle whose limits the expert say-so contains. His result maps Elenchus states to bases in nonmonotonic multi-succedent logic, meeting Containment and spelling out inferential links.
arxiv-2603-07274: Draziotis and Gkogkou study a non-modular form of the Short Integer Solution problem over whole numbers. The task is to find a short nonzero vector that a random integer matrix sends to zero. They show that solving random cases even sometimes would yield a fast method for approximating a classic hard lattice problem in the worst case. The link turns average-case hardness into worst-case hardness for this integer setting.
arxiv-2603-07474: Xu and colleagues probe whether language models recover hypernym knowledge from images when explicit evidence is stripped away. In a vision-language setup with frozen encoder and language model, only the mappings between them are learned. The models recover hypernym knowledge and generalize even when training shows no evidence of a hypernym at all. The effect survives counterfactual image-label swaps only when categories stay visually coherent within themselves.
arxiv-2603-07974: Wang presents ZK-ACE, a zero-knowledge authorization scheme for post-quantum blockchains. It replaces bulky signature objects with identity-bound zero-knowledge claims. Post-quantum signatures leave kilobyte-scale artifacts, and verifying them inside zero-knowledge circuits merely shifts the cost. Given a deterministic identity primitive as a black box, the prover shows in zero knowledge that an identity matching an on-chain pledge authorized it. No signature object is made or verified on-chain, and proofs run far smaller than in-circuit signature verification.
arxiv-2603-08074: Aichholzer and colleagues analyze a geometric balancing game from Spencer in 1977. Take n lines in the plane, with a box in each cell. Alice starts by placing pebbles in every box. Then Bob picks a line, and Alice must choose a side. She removes one pebble from each box on that side and adds one to each on the other side. Bob wins if any box empties. The authors find the minimum pebble count that lets Alice stop Bob from ever winning, and show it is computable in polynomial time.
arxiv-2603-08174: Shen and colleagues build a foundation for multimodal large language models in the electromagnetic domain, where prevailing approaches drift from the native MLLM paradigm toward task-specific pipelines. Three challenges block progress: scarce paired signal-text datasets, missing benchmarks for EM signal-to-text tasks, and fragility at low signal-to-noise ratios, where key features blur. Their tripartite contribution starts with EM-100k, a dataset of over 100,000 EM signal-text pairs. It adds standardized evaluation and a model design aimed at low-SNR robustness.
arxiv-2603-08274: Roig asks how much large language models hallucinate when answering questions grounded in provided documents. Reliable measurement has been hampered by benchmarks on static datasets, judges based on language models with known biases, or test scales too small for statistical confidence. Using RIKER, a ground-truth-first evaluation methodology enabling deterministic scoring without human labels, the author runs over 172 billion tokens of testing across 35 open-weight models. Even the best models invent answers at a non-trivial rate, and that rate rises steeply with context length.
arxiv-2603-08674: Mengyi Shan and colleagues animate two people talking face to face in 3D from one mixed audio track. Past tools make floating heads like a video call, missing the shared space, gaze, and relative poses of a real chat. Their dual-stream design splits the audio by speaker, models gaze and pose from text cues, and trains on over two million curated chat pairs.
arxiv-2603-08874: Jose de Jesus Bernal-Alvarado and David Delepine argue that gauge physics explains why parts of Poland and Bohemia escaped the Black Death. Classical spread models cannot explain untouched interiors while neighbors collapsed. Their SU(4) gauge model of plague lineages yields safe zones with a Bessel radial profile, matching the observed anomaly size for nearly all admissible parameter draws.
arxiv-2603-09574: Milo Carroll and colleagues present Sensor-Conditioned Diffusion Policies, which teach humanoid locomotion from offline data using only onboard sensors. Older methods need privileged full-body states and costly state estimation. Their training mixes what the model sees, sensor histories, with what it must predict, privileged future state-action paths. That forces it to infer motion it cannot directly observe. Added steps curb train-deploy mismatch, and in simulation the policies rival full-state baselines.
arxiv-2603-09874: Tien Anh Pham and coauthors introduce MissBench, a benchmark for emotion and sentiment models when some input channels go missing. Real systems lose text, sound or video at uneven rates, yet standard tests assume all three are present alike. MissBench sets shared and uneven missing rate rules on four data sets. Two new scores track fairness across channels and balance in how training treats each channel.
arxiv-2603-09974: Aleksei Rozanov, Arvind Renganathan and Vipin Kumar improve global estimates of land carbon flux with a task aware learning framework. Ground flux towers are sparse and regionally biased, so data driven products often fail in new regions. TAM-RL couples space time representation learning with an encoder decoder guided by the carbon balance equation. Across many tower sites in varied biomes, it cuts error and much raises explained variance over leading products.
arxiv-2603-10074: Mihir Sahasrabudhe builds a minimal task that isolates how neural networks learn conditional structure. A selector token resolves a K fold ambiguity in the target, so full knowledge needs that token. The model first learns the plain marginal, sitting on a plateau whose height is set by the ambiguity. Gradient noise holds it there, while a selector routing head quietly assembles until a sharp collective jump completes the conditional.
arxiv-2603-10174: Eric Chen and coauthors help underwater robots find rare coral species by reading the habitat around them, not just the target. A survey vehicle with limited battery cannot search a whole reef, and sparse target sightings give weak guidance. Their method uses patch level DINOv2 embeddings from one labelled image to spot both the species and its denser, smoother context online. Offline trials on real reef imagery from St. John support the approach.
arxiv-2603-10274: Javier Blanco-Romero and co-authors build a service that sends quantum random entropy to small embedded devices over post-quantum secure channels. A Quantis device feeds the server, which offers direct quantum entropy or a mix with the system pool. On ESP32-class clients, the team adds secure DTLS links to the CoAP stack and a fast local pool for the delivered entropy. Benchmarks show the fully post-quantum setup finishing handshakes faster than the classical baseline, making strong entropy practical on tiny hardware.
arxiv-2603-10374: Advait Bhat and co-authors study how co-writing with AI changes how people engage with ideas, through interviews and a large trace of real sessions. Reading suggestions and deciding whether to take them became central to writing, crowding out the writer's own ideation and drafting. Writers often met suggestions before finishing their own thinking, so the AI seeded directions they then built on. Yet they felt fully in control and did not notice the influence. The authors call this reactive writing, an evaluation-first practice open to AI bias.
arxiv-2603-10774: Zhi-Gang Wang and Yang Liu analyze hidden-charm pentaquark candidates in the J/psi Sigma mass spectrum, using QCD sum rules within a diquark picture. They build diquark-diquark-antiquark currents with light quarks in two octets, and study the singly strange hidden-charm states systematically. The work yields the mass spectrum for three sets of quantum numbers, with isospin one and negative parity. The authors point to two decay processes, through Sigma_b and Xi_b channels, where these predicted states could be searched for.
arxiv-2603-10974: A. Kumashita and coauthors report high-precision heat-capacity measurements of a submonolayer of helium-3 adsorbed on highly crystalline graphite, probing its commensurate-incommensurate transition. Below 1 K, two striped domain-wall phases appear: one with variable wall spacing and heat capacity linear in temperature, from one-dimensional phonons along the walls, and one with fixed spacing. The fixed-spacing phase melts into the other at a critical density through a second-order transition, consistent with a quantum nematic state in the variable-spacing phase.
arxiv-2603-11174: Yutong Chen and coauthors present GGPT, a point transformer that grounds feed-forward sparse-view 3D reconstruction in geometry. It fixes flaws that come from predicting dense point maps straight from images. An improved structure-from-motion pipeline based on dense feature matching first estimates accurate camera poses and partial point clouds from the sparse views. GGPT then refines dense point maps under partial-geometry supervision, restoring fine detail and filling textureless gaps. The model also works across architectures and datasets.
arxiv-2603-11274: Atieh Taheri and coauthors test whether talking with an AI mediator helps people spot ableist microaggressions, everyday slights that remain common yet hard to confront. One hundred sixty participants rated cases before and after one of four conditions: a talk nudged toward bias, a talk nudged toward inclusion, an unguided talk, or plain reading. Dialogue beat reading overall. Biased nudges sharpened the line between bias and neutrality while raising negativity. Inclusive nudges were taken up as scaffolding, while biased ones were often rejected.
arxiv-2603-11974: Deck and co-authors propose NormCoRe, a framework translating human experiments into multi-agent AI studies of norms. Norms shape how agent systems settle shared decisions in fairness-sensitive areas. Existing work treats agents as human stand-ins, leaving group norm dynamics unexamined. NormCoRe maps each layer of a human study design onto an agent study, with systematic records. They test it on a classic distributive justice study run under a veil of ignorance. Agent judgments differ from human baselines and shift with the base model and the language used.
arxiv-2603-12274: Bae, Malberg, Galang, Retterath, and Groh built DIALECTIC, a multi-agent system that screens startups for investors. Venture investors face far more pitches than they can study with full diligence. The system first gathers facts on a startup and sorts them into a hierarchical question tree. Agents then draft arguments for and against the deal and refine them through simulated debate. Only the most convincing arguments survive that critique loop. Numeric scores let investors rank the flow, and backtests on real deals matched human VC precision.
arxiv-2603-12574: Yohei Hayamizu and co-authors give robotic guide dogs a way to speak with their handlers. Such robots help blind users avoid obstacles and find their way. Plain dialogue add-ons fail here, since speech must track a fast-changing scene. Their system uses large language models to voice both route plans and scene details. That lets handler and robot make joint choices as they move. A human study tested wording plans, and a simulation checked route speed and accuracy.
arxiv-2603-12774: Alexandra Blessing and Mazyar Ghani Varzaneh study synchronization by noise for equations driven by fractional Brownian motion. Such systems are non-Markovian, which makes the usual tools harder to apply. When the system has a negative top Lyapunov exponent, they show a weak form of synchronization occurs. Their proof uses random dynamical systems and the support of an invariant measure. The result covers Hurst index values across the full range from 0 to 1.
arxiv-2603-13274: Gianluigi Silvestri and Edoardo Cetin introduce Truncated-Reasoning Self-Distillation, or TRSD, for reasoning language models. Long chain-of-thought traces give strong results but cost a great deal of compute. TRSD trains a student to answer well from only a truncated prefix of a reasoning trace. A frozen teacher first builds a full trace and an answer distribution as the target. Across benchmarks and token budgets, TRSD kept accuracy high under truncated inference. Trained models also wrote shorter traces on their own, cutting inference costs further.
arxiv-2603-13774: Hai Lan and co-authors propose AgenticScholar, an agentic data management system for scholarly corpora. Managing the growing corpus challenges representation, reasoning, and efficient analysis at scale. Existing RAG and document analytics systems cannot achieve all query types at once, they argue. AgenticScholar joins three layers: one for structure-aware knowledge, one for hybrid query planning centered on an LLM, and one for unified execution. It translates natural language queries into executable DAG plans autonomously for end-to-end reasoning.
arxiv-2603-14074: Zheng, Dewil, and Arias add uncertainty estimates to self-supervised super-resolution of satellite images. Paired low- and high-resolution training data rarely exist, so recent methods learn from burst shots of the same scene. Those methods give no sense of where the rebuilt image may be wrong. A new loss, read through decision theory, yields the posterior mean and variance as best estimates. On a synthetic SkySat dataset, the error bars match those of supervised methods.
arxiv-2603-14174: Chen and Jiménez compute the fixed-time spatial covariance of the KPZ equation with a flat starting profile. With Malliavin calculus and a Clark-Ocone form, they find the far-field decay as distance grows. The covariance falls off like a Gaussian in space, with a rate set by time and a factor from the flat heat equation. That shape contrasts with the narrow-wedge case, where decay is a slow power law. The result is the first exact covariance formula of this kind for flat data.
arxiv-2603-14674: Habib, Smith and Smith probe how Herman Melville's reading echoes in his own writing. Documented lists of books Melville owned or read anchor the study. Passages from his works face passages from his library. Texts split at sentence level and into fixed five-word chunks. BERTScore then grades semantic closeness between the pairs. Scores act as hints of alignment, not proof of reuse. Known expert-flagged matches surface under the method. Fresh candidate pairs emerge for closer human study, they report.
arxiv-2603-14774: Di and co-authors compute electric dipole moments for leptons and the neutron in the N-B-LSSM. Standard Model dipole moments sit far below lab limits. New CP-violating phases could lift them into view. The model extends the MSSM with right-handed neutrinos and extra singlet Higgs fields. One-loop formulas come via the mass insertion approximation. Lepton and quark moments depend on new gauge couplings and CP phases. Numeric scans show dipole data squeeze the allowed parameter space hard.
arxiv-2603-15274: Huelamo and co-authors resolve the very faint object IRAM 04191+1522 into a close proto-brown dwarf binary candidate. ALMA images at fine resolution show two sources split by about 11 astronomical units. The eastern source is brighter and more extended. Gas data reveal a rotating circumbinary disk of about 27 units in radius. A fit to the velocity pattern gives a total mass near 50 Jupiter masses, with wide error bars. Radio data from the VLA show one object with a jet-like spectral index.
arxiv-2603-15374: Zhang and co-authors present SpecDepth, a light adaptation of vision foundation models for depth estimation in colonoscopy. Models trained on natural images fail here, not from a meaning gap but from a frequency shift. Colonoscopy images lack the sharp edges and textures the models lean on. A learnable wavelet module boosts the faded high-frequency parts of feature maps. This low-level fix keeps the pretrained geometry skills intact. On C3VD and SimCol3D, the method set state-of-the-art scores with very few added parameters.
arxiv-2603-15774: Marikkar, Awais, and Atito cut the compute cost of whole slide image analysis. Giant slide scans make end-to-end training impractical in pathology. Standard pipelines freeze feature extractors trained on natural images. In-domain pretraining helps but costs heavily and stays task-blind. Their eWSI method joins light fine-tuning with multiple instance learning. End-to-end training then runs on slide-level tasks directly. Tests span seven tasks on Camelyon16, TCGA, and BRACS data. eWSI matched or beat frozen in-domain extractors at lower cost.
arxiv-2603-15974: Frøseth generalizes a tax neutrality result across a full ownership tax stack. A flat wealth tax alone shifts wealth drift without tilting portfolios. He adds corporate, capital income, dividend, and wealth taxes together. Each tax bends the wealth drift in its own pattern. The diffusion term stays untouched by all four taxes. Neutrality survives when three stated conditions hold at once. Shielding ties equity and debt treatment back into symmetry. Calibrated to Norway, one distortion dominates all others. Uneven wealth tax assessment tilts portfolios about 300-fold more.
arxiv-2603-16474: Burlakov and co-authors recheck Monte Carlo tree search for database query planning. Recent systems claimed big wins over classic optimizers. Those systems lean on learned cost models. The team's rerun finds the claims often fail on varied workloads. Learned cost models break down off their training data. Their new framework uses the database's own cost model instead. A new selection rule, Extreme UCT, steers the search. It beat learned rivals and a top optimizer on complex joins.
arxiv-2603-16574: Malsburg and Padó test transformers as models of human sentence reading. Agreement attraction errors reveal how readers process syntax. The team scores eleven autoregressive models with a surprisal link. Configurations cover more ground than prior studies. For prepositional phrase cases, model times track human data. For object-extracted relative clauses, performance drops sharply. Models also split from each other there. None copies the asymmetric interference pattern humans show.
arxiv-2603-16674: Jaikin-Zapirain, Souza, and Zalesski detect free products from profinite completions. Their groups are fundamental groups of graphs of virtually free groups. Edge groups in the graph are virtually cyclic. If the group is LERF, it splits as a free product exactly when its completion does. The split there is a free profinite product. One-ended free factors can also be read off the completion. A rigid word in a free group is then universally rigid.
arxiv-2603-16774: Brazas and co-authors revisit a question about tree-like paths in metric spaces. Hambly and Lyons showed that Lipschitz tree-like paths form an equivalence relation on paths of bounded variation. They asked whether the same holds without the Lipschitz condition. The authors show it does not. Once that condition is dropped, the tree-like relation stops being transitive, so it is no longer an equivalence relation. Their counterexample comes from an explicit fractal construction in the plane.
arxiv-2603-16874: Gausen and co-authors argue that chat AI should state it is AI whenever a user asks directly. Users often cannot tell whether they face a human or a machine, and unclear identity invites misplaced trust or fraud. Laws require self identification but say little about live conversation. Interface labels can be omitted, and provenance tools need shared infrastructure. The team tested deployed text and voice systems in normal, role play, and adversarial settings. Disclosure was often high at baseline but fell sharply in role play and under attack.
arxiv-2603-16974: Zhang and co-authors enrich multimodal knowledge graphs by turning images into text. Large image collections are hard to curate, and ambiguous visuals like logos are often dropped. Their pipeline, Beyond Images, retrieves more entity related images, converts all visuals into text descriptions, and fuses those texts into short entity summaries. These summaries can replace or augment the text side of standard models. Across three public datasets, the authors report gains up to 7 percent in Hits@1. On ambiguous logos, gains were far larger.
arxiv-2603-17074: Runwal and co-authors present PRISM, a large empirical study of mid training for language models. Mid training is the stage between pretraining and reinforcement learning. Across seven base models, mid training on about 27B quality tokens gave steady gains. Math scores rose 15 to 40 points, with smaller gains in code and science. Data mix mattered most at mid training, not at the RL stage. Mid training rewrites over 90 percent of weights, while RL touches about 5 percent. Only mid trained models improved well under RL.
arxiv-2603-17274: Chatterjee and Liu propose a phonon polarization filter built from magnetic topological insulators. The surface of such a solid shows a phonon Hall viscosity, the analog of axion electrodynamics. This effect creates an interface phonon mode below the bulk mode in frequency. The mode carries one set circular polarization, so only matching phonons stay confined at the interface. The authors also build a scattering treatment for sound injected from a normal insulator.
arxiv-2603-17374: Zhao and co-authors present InfoShot, a frame sampler for long-video understanding with vision-language models. Keeping few frames risks dropping brief but key events. InfoShot splits a video into shots, then keeps two frames per shot. One frame shows the main content, and one catches odd changes inside the shot. A new synthetic test, SynFlash, checks sub-second events. Anomaly hits and video question scores improved, they report.
arxiv-2603-17474: Zang and co-authors present DACSM, a framework for unsupervised domain adaptation with cross-attention. Style and scale gaps often break feature alignment between source and target domains. Their design adds controlled noise to attention, pushing the model to track content over style. A second module aligns features across several resolutions at once. On VisDA-2017 the method beat a strong baseline by up to 2.3 points, they report. The truck class gained 5.9 points.
arxiv-2603-17574: Masson and co-authors run a blind search for molecules in 14 transiting exoplanet atmospheres. They mine 50 SPIRou transits from large programs and public archives. An automated pipeline pairs nested-sampling retrievals with cross-correlation checks. Water and carbon monoxide detections held up in three hot planets, they report. Hints of hydrogen sulfide appeared in two more. Null results still yield firm upper limits for the rest.
arxiv-2603-17674: Liubimov and Gorsky solve a Russian-doll model of superconductivity exactly. The model breaks time-reversal symmetry and its renormalization group runs in cycles. In the one-pair sector they map localized, fractal, and delocalized phases. A quantum number from the Bethe ansatz counts the cycles and labels towers of states. That number works as an order parameter, they show. The fractal phase grows from this cyclic flow in a clean, deterministic system.
arxiv-2603-17974: Lbath sets out a doctoral plan for building large test sets for flaws in whole code bases. Current sets focus on single functions and miss real, runnable flaws across files. His generator would plant real-like flaws in real projects and build working proof exploits for each one. A paired loop would pit planting agents against hunting agents. The aim is sharper training and testing of repo-level flaw detectors.
arxiv-2603-18074: Ma and co-authors adapt technical-service LLM agents with latent logic, noise cuts, and hybrid rewards. Service tickets hide decision logic, hold noisy single replies, and cost much to score. Their framework adds planning-aware trajectory data and dual-filtered ground truths. A hybrid reward joins a reranker with an LLM judge. On real cloud service tasks, the tuned Qwen3-4B hit the best score and a 46.63% production adoption rate.
arxiv-2603-18174: Liu and co-authors build conflict-free policy languages for systems driven by probabilistic ML signals. Crisp rule conflicts are decidable, but embedding and classifier signals can both fire on one query. They map a three-level hierarchy: SAT for crisp rules, spherical caps for embeddings, and undecidable classifier cases. A temperature-scaled softmax splits embedding space into Voronoi regions where co-firing cannot occur. The tools ship in the Semantic Router DSL for LLM routing.
arxiv-2603-18274: Park, Ueno, and Tanimura present sbml4md, a tool that builds system-bath models from atom motion data with machine learning. It pulls the terms of a multi-mode Brownian model from MD paths, with no hand-tuned fits. The learning step picks up mode shapes, mode links, and bath time traces for each mode. Those terms feed exact-style equations for nonlinear spectra of real liquids. This update adds links between molecules, which widens the range of use.
arxiv-2603-18674: Al Bazzal and Togni study t-tone colorings of two planar graph classes. Each vertex gets a set of t colors, and near vertices must share few colors. They fully pin down the 2-tone chromatic number for subcubic outerplanar graphs. For the 3-tone number of the same class, they give a sharp upper bound. For Halin graphs, every cubic one with at least six vertices is 2-tone 7-colorable. They also bound the 2-tone number for Halin graphs with any maximum degree.
arxiv-2603-18974: Kuca surveys forty years of work on joint ergodicity in math dynamics. The topic asks when a combined average of several maps settles to the product of single averages. Recent years have brought sharp progress on this question. The survey sums up the new results and the tools behind them. It also lays out open problems and the main blocks that remain. The piece goes with a talk honoring Vitaly Bergelson at seventy-five. It aims to guide readers through a fast-moving field.
arxiv-2603-19474: Wang and co-authors build TRACE, a diffusion model that rebuilds dense GPS tracks from sparse ones. Real tracks often have few, uneven points due to weak sampling and poor coverage. TRACE adds a state propagation step inside the denoising process. That memory lets the model reuse past steps to fix hard segments. On several real data sets, TRACE beats prior methods by over 26 percent in accuracy. Inference cost stays low, and the code is public.
arxiv-2603-19974: Liu and co-authors study a stealthy attack on autonomous coding agents that use the OpenClaw platform. OpenClaw lets third parties add behavioral guidance through skills loaded at startup. The attack hides harmful narratives inside these guidance files. Harmful steps get framed as routine best practice, not as blunt commands. The agent then absorbs them into its working context without suspicion. The team built 26 malicious skills across 13 attack types. These cover credential theft, workspace damage, privilege gains, and backdoor installs.
arxiv-2603-20074: Khadka and Santosh adapt Mamba-style state space models for image tasks with multi-filter scanning. Vision data is not a simple sequence, so plain scans add redundancy and warp spatial links. Their MFil-Mamba backbone gives each scan its own filter. Each pass then gathers distinct, context-rich spatial information. An adaptive weighting step fuses the scan outputs. The model beat leading rivals across several benchmarks. These covered image classification, object detection, and both instance and semantic segmentation. The tiny version also held up well in their tests.
arxiv-2603-20174: Capogrosso and Magno bring tiny machine learning aboard CubeSat missions for Earth observation. Small satellites cannot send all raw imagery down or run heavy analysis onboard. Their pipeline optimizes convolutional networks for a microcontroller with a neural accelerator. Structured pruning shrinks the models step by step. Post-training INT8 quantization cuts precision to save energy. Operator mapping then fits the chip's mixed compute units. Four models were tested on three Earth observation datasets. The setup aims at accurate, low-power image classification within strict CubeSat limits.
arxiv-2603-20274: Sterkenburg examines Solomonoff induction, a classic approach to universal prediction built on computability. He presents its main idea as an attempt to meet two plausible demands on a universal predictor. He then shows the attempt fails, using a generalized diagonal argument due to Putnam. The chapter also weighs claimed gains of the approach. These include a foundation for Occam's razor and an ideal guide for machine learning methods.
arxiv-2603-20374: Géron and co-authors present DETECT, a pipeline for measuring detection limits in Rubin Observatory images. Stars near death can vary before exploding, and Rubin will watch for this. Bright host galaxies, though, make faint targets hard to measure reliably. DETECT injects fake sources, subtracts images, and forces photometry at set spots. This yields detection thresholds tailored to each target location. Tests used simulated Rubin data and 15 targets from early data. False positives clustered at low signal levels and vanished at higher ones.
arxiv-2603-20474: Ray presents NGCG, a neural and symbolic pipeline that finds conservation laws in data with no false positives. The method splits dynamics learning from law search. A multi-restart step learns a near constant latent feature from the data. Symbolic tools then pull out closed form laws from that feature. A strict constancy gate and a diversity filter drop fake laws. On nine test systems the pipeline found all true laws. It also gave no law for the five systems that have none.
arxiv-2603-20674: Priyanka and co-authors survey carbon farming across many fields in one unified treatment. Carbon farming uses farm practices that store carbon in soil and plants. It also cuts emissions from cultivation itself. They claim full use on India's cropland could offset half its transport emissions. The survey covers soil carbon basics and best practices by crop. It also reviews measurement and credit checks, carbon markets, and policy design. Co-benefits and trade offs get a full look.
arxiv-2603-20874: Aggarwal and co-authors derive solar wind speed and coronal electron density from radio signal broadening. Spacecraft radio signals blur as they pass through near Sun plasma. Past methods fixed the turbulence index in advance. Their framework allows any index, so no fixed regime is assumed. They apply it to Akatsuki X-band data from the 2016 and 2022 conjunctions. The density results match known coronal models. Fast wind speeds agree well, while slow wind shows small shifts tied to uneven turbulence.
arxiv-2603-20974: Pal studies finite sample smeariness for data that live on spheres. On curved spaces, the usual limit results need a correction tied to curvature. He shows that for smooth distributions on spheres, this Type I smeariness cannot be avoided. In higher dimensions the effect grows and can become very large. He builds explicit estimators of the Fréchet function Hessian. These give corrected one sample and two sample tests with chi-square limits. In experiments, the tests match bootstrap corrections and run much faster.
arxiv-2603-21174: Lozano and co-authors introduce Dissimilar Span Detection, a task that explains text similarity scores. Semantic textual similarity tools usually give one score, which hides which words drive the judgment down. Their task finds the spans that differ in meaning between two texts. They release the Span Similarity Dataset, built with model help and human checks. Baselines include unsupervised methods based on LIME and SHAP, language models, and a supervised method. Language models and the supervised method do best, but scores stay low. The spans also improve paraphrase detection.
arxiv-2603-21274: Sygrimis and Tsironis show how gain can make graphene plasmons propagate without loss. Graphene plasmons confine fields tightly and tune electrically, but ohmic loss kills them fast. They embed the graphene sheet in an active dielectric that supplies gain. From the full Maxwell model, they derive closed form rules for the gain that makes the propagation constant real. The rules use the complex conductivity of graphene and the nearby media directly. Finite element simulations confirm the trends for single and double layer structures, with and without gain.
arxiv-2603-21374: Sun and co-authors build a hybrid quantum-classical branch-and-price method for intra-day electric vehicle charging schedules. Tight charger capacity and short dwell times make the scheduling hard. They model it as a partition coloring problem, with conflict graphs for time and resource clashes. The pricing subproblem is a maximum independent set, recast as a QUBO and solved by quantum-annealing-inspired algorithms. On large, hard instances, the hybrid closes optimality gaps that the pure Gurobi baseline leaves open.
arxiv-2603-22074: Esteban and co-authors introduce MIHT, a decision tree method for time series classification. Time series often vary in length and carry many variables, which trips up standard models. MIHT views each series as a bag of subseries, borrowing from multiple instance learning. An incremental Hoeffding tree then separates the telling segments from noise. The learned tree stays compact and readable. It points to the variables and segments that matter most. The authors report MIHT beats 11 top rival methods on 28 public datasets. The wins include high-dimensional data.
arxiv-2603-22474: Senthilkumar and Menzies ask large language models to label data for software engineering optimization. Such labels are slow and costly to get from scarce human experts. The authors find model labels fail on high-dimensional, multi-objective tasks when used one at a time. Their fix, SynthCore, polls several isolated model sessions and merges their views into an ensemble of few-shot learners. On 49 tasks the ensemble beat leading search methods. All labels came from models, with no human input.
arxiv-2603-22574: Amin and co-authors present GIFT, a framework that helps robot reward functions travel to new settings. Rewards learned from demonstrations often latch onto surface quirks and fail elsewhere. GIFT instead asks a language model to infer the person's real intent, by contrasting liked and disliked behavior. At test time it matches new states to training states that mean the same thing under that intent. On tabletop tasks with unseen objects, GIFT beats similarity-based rivals. It also transfers to a real robot arm.
arxiv-2603-22674: Ma and co-authors design a dashboard that gives instructors insight into student chats with AI. Those chats hold much of the help-seeking in a course, yet teachers cannot see them. Reading raw logs for a whole class is impractical and raises privacy concerns. Their dashboard shows session-level summaries made by a reflection AI instead. It reports the path of each session, usage patterns, and risks. The team co-designed the tool with instructors and students. A formative test found it cut sensemaking effort and eased privacy worries.
arxiv-2603-22774: Chung and co-authors show that CPUs, not GPUs, often slow multi-GPU language model serving. In their study, GPUs sit idle because CPUs cannot keep them fed. Signs include late kernel launches, stalled communication, and slow tokenization. The problem worsens in agent serving, where long contexts raise CPU work. Prefix cache reuse cuts GPU work at the same time. Adding CPU cores proves a cheap fix. Under moderate load, well-fed setups cut time to first token by 1.47 to 7.11 times.
arxiv-2603-23074: Kuruc and co-authors modify radial basis function interpolation to cut wiggles near jumps. Classic methods oscillate near discontinuities in one and two dimensions. Their change makes the shape parameter depend on the data. Near a jump, the parameter grows toward infinity. The kernels then act almost like delta functions at those spots. Smoothness indicators flag the jumps from grid or scattered data. The authors prove the interpolation matrix stays invertible. Tests show far fewer wiggles, with smooth-region accuracy intact.
arxiv-2603-23374: Bao and four co-authors tackle conditional coverage in conformal prediction. A prediction set should cover the truth at the promised rate for each case, not just on average. Past tools calibrated one fixed set shape, which limits how sets can bend. Their framework, MOPI, optimizes over a flexible family of set shapes at calibration time. A minimax setup keeps it tied to low squared coverage error. Theory gives oracle bounds and an optimal error rate. Tests on tricky distributions show tighter sets than rival methods.
arxiv-2603-23474: Damião and five co-authors audit search engines and chatbots for political skew before elections. They built a privacy-safe bot method to query four search engines and two language models. About 4,360 election queries spanned five EU states and 15 US counties. In Europe, results named far-right groups more than polls or past votes suggest. In the US, Google leaned toward Republican-salient topics while rivals leaned Democratic. Chatbot replies sat closer to balance, with some far-right and Green overreach. The team urges audits of such platforms.
arxiv-2603-23674: Pantoni and 25 co-authors map aromatic dust emission at the heart of Centaurus A with JWST. The MIRI instrument resolves the inner few hundred light-years down to a handful of light-years per pixel. Emission gathers in a ring with bright knots, plus one PAH-poor patch near the jet. Band ratios there point to open, worn molecules stripped of hydrogen by shocks. The ring shows the strongest features, while the nucleus glow stays diluted by bright continuum light. Active nuclei plainly rework their nearby dust.
arxiv-2603-23974: Ma and co-authors introduce a sensing method that lets machine vision work with very few photons. Normal systems use thousands of photons per pixel, so very dark scenes are hard. Their method, photon-aware neuromorphic sensing, trains the optics and the processor together with the photon budget in mind. In tests, it classified FashionMNIST images with only 4.9 detected photons per inference, at 73 percent accuracy. On MNIST it reached 86 percent with 8.6 photons. Simulations extend the idea to event detection and image reconstruction.
arxiv-2603-24874: Lo Piparo and co-authors study adaptive resource and memory control for quantum entanglement distribution. Repeater nodes face random traffic and finite memory coherence. Entanglement arrives as Werner states that decohere in memory, while requests follow Poisson or bursty arrivals. A queueing framework couples memory behaviour with congestion-dependent service. Fixed cutoff policies force a strict fidelity-latency trade-off. Queue-aware control adjusts memory cutoffs and parallel channel counts on the fly. Resource scaling adds capacity without hurting quality.
arxiv-2603-25074: Jiang and co-authors erase unwanted concepts from a new kind of image generator. Single-stream diffusion transformers mix text and image tokens in one sequence with shared weights. Old erasure methods, built for split designs, often wreck output on these models. Their Z-Erase first splits the update path so prior methods can run safely. A guided modulation step then balances removal against keeping the rest of the image skill. They prove the method settles at a balanced point. Tests show clean erasure with no collapse.
arxiv-2603-25174: Duverney and Shiokawa prove that two limit functions built from Stern polynomials take independent values. Stern polynomials grow from the classic Stern sequence. Certain subsequences settle toward functions H_k inside the unit disk. A power-shifted copy of each function also appears. Using Mahler's method, the pair shows the two values are algebraically independent at any nonzero algebraic point. That means no polynomial relation with algebraic weights ties them together. The result links a counting sequence to deep number theory.
arxiv-2603-25374: Stripelis and co-authors federate document search so private stores never pool their text. Standard retrieval-augmented generation assumes one central pile of documents. Their Flower-based system searches each silo on site. Merging and answer writing run inside an attested, sealed compute space. That keeps remote model use private even if the server is nosy or breached. A cascade trick can also call a public third-party model for extra context. It does so without leaking the private material.
arxiv-2603-25674: Walsh and Ivan test whether an LLM-based scoring system is swayed by factors outside the target skill. The system scores short open responses on a situational judgment test. The authors pad answers with empty text, add spelling errors, and vary writing polish. The system stayed mostly robust to those changes, they report. Copying large passages into an answer lowered its score. Off-topic answers were penalized heavily. The authors say the results support careful design of LLM scoring tools for real tests.
arxiv-2603-25774: Wakaura and Tanimae present catalytic quantum error correction, a new way to recover quantum states from noise. Standard correction fails once noise passes about one percent and costs many extra qubits. Their method uses catalytic coherence amplification, an effect from the resource theory of coherence. It restores a known target state from noisy copies with no noise threshold, as long as key modes survive. In an effective model, fidelity topped 0.99 across 200 noise settings. A small exact test under dephasing also showed real recovery, though shallow circuits drain the catalyst.
arxiv-2603-25974: Li, Ma, and Ni propose a new liquid xenon detector for medical PET imaging. Liquid xenon offers fine energy resolution, fast light, and true 3D position sensing. Their single-phase chamber reads both scintillation and ionization light for low-noise gain. Built-in depth sensing comes from the ionization readout. Monte Carlo tests compare it with standard LYSO crystal scanners. Xenon loses on raw stopping power but wins on photopeak purity. Scattered events are rejected better. Point sources reconstruct at about one millimeter width, versus four for LYSO.
arxiv-2603-26174: Wang and co-authors present CREval, an automatic way to grade creative image editing under complex instructions. Scoring by large models alone is opaque and often incomplete. CREval instead grades edits through a question-answer pipeline that can be inspected. Its bench, CREval-Bench, holds over 800 editing samples and 13,000 test queries. Tasks span three categories and nine creative dimensions. Closed models beat open ones on these tasks, the authors find. All models still struggle to complete such edits well. User studies show the scores track human judgment closely.
